title: Senior asks: someone sends GET ?action=DELETE&file=a.csv. What happens?
explain: handle() makes the action lower case, so DELETE is accepted as delete. Then checkAction() compares the real HTTP method: it must be DELETE, but it is GET, so the answer is 405. The method check is what stops a link or a crawler from deleting files.

title: Senior asks: index.php sends home.html with file_get_contents(). What is the downside?
options: PHP runs for every page load, and there are no cache headers
The HTML is run as PHP code and can leak secrets
The jQuery file can no longer load
Browsers cannot show HTML from PHP
explain: file_get_contents() only reads the text. It does not run it, so there is no leak. But every visit starts PHP, and Response sends no ETag or cache headers. A static file lets the web server do this fast. It is fine for a small project, but static files are better served by the server.

title: Senior asks: write() checks is_file() first to answer 201 or 200. Two clients create the same new file at the same time. What can happen?
options: Both get 201, and the last write wins
An exception is thrown for the second client
The file has mixed content from both
explain: Both calls see no file, so both return 201. LOCK_EX stops mixed content: the writes run one after the other and the last one wins. The check and the write are two steps, so it is a small race. Here it is only a wrong status code, so it is acceptable. Do not use this pattern for money or ids.

title: storage/ has: b.csv, A.json, a.csv, notes.txt, .tmp.json. What does listFiles() return?
explain: scandir() sorts by byte value: '.' comes before 'A', and 'A' before 'a'. Only the extension is checked, so hidden files like .tmp.json are listed too. Only notes.txt is dropped. If you want to hide dot files, add str_starts_with($name, '.') to the check.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: switch compares with == (loose), so "1" == 1 is true. match compares with === (strict), so "1" does not match 1 and default runs. Without default, match throws UnhandledMatchError. Prefer match when types matter.

title: What does this print?
explain: clone is shallow. $b is a new Box, but $b->data points to the same stdClass object as $a->data. Changing it through $b changes it for $a too. For a deep copy, write __clone() and clone the inner object there, or use readonly value objects.

title: What does Node print?
explain: NaN is never equal to itself with ===, and indexOf uses ===, so it returns -1. includes() uses a different rule (SameValueZero) and finds NaN. To test for NaN use Number.isNaN(x).

title: "vendor/pkg": "~2.3.1" allows which versions?
explain: ~ lets the last number you wrote go up. ~2.3.1 means >=2.3.1 <2.4.0, so only patch updates. ~2.3 would mean >=2.3 <3.0. The caret ^2.3.1 means >=2.3.1 <3.0.0. Use ~ when you want only bug fixes.
